lead: This week in tech highlights significant advancements in AI, startup funding, and innovative product launches, particularly within the Australian tech ecosystem.

stories.title: Ultrahuman raised $70m to turn its ring into a computer
stories.summary: Ultrahuman has successfully raised $70 million in funding, aiming to transform its smart ring from a mere health tracker into a fully functional computing device. The investment will allow the company to expand its capabilities, focusing on software development that enhances user experience beyond health metrics. This move reflects a growing trend in wearable technology towards multifunctional devices.

stories.title: Thinking Machines is in talks to raise $6bn
stories.summary: Thinking Machines Lab is reportedly seeking to raise between $5 billion to $6 billion, indicating strong investor interest in AI-driven technologies. The pre-money valuation is expected to be at least $40 billion, showcasing the confidence in the company's potential to innovate within the AI space. Accel, a long-time investor, continues to support this ambitious funding round.

stories.title: OpenAI says it reached its goal of creating an automated research intern
stories.summary: OpenAI has announced that it has successfully developed an automated research intern, a significant milestone in AI research capabilities. This advancement aims to streamline research processes and improve efficiency in information gathering and analysis. The company plans to enhance this technology further, with goals set for a more advanced version by 2028.

stories.title: Anthropic will reportedly list days before the US midterm elections
stories.summary: Anthropic is preparing for a stock market debut, with plans to market its offering just before the upcoming US midterm elections. This strategic timing could influence investor interest and market dynamics, especially given the company's focus on AI safety and ethics. The expected valuation and investor backing highlight the growing importance of AI in the financial sector.

stories.title: Nscale is selling Figure $3.5bn of compute and buying a stake in it
stories.summary: Nscale has entered a significant deal to sell computing power worth at least $3.5 billion to Figure, while also acquiring an equity stake in the company. This partnership is set to leverage Nscale's extensive computing resources, particularly Nvidia GPUs, to enhance Figure's capabilities in the AI sector. Such collaborations are indicative of the growing interdependencies in tech-driven industries.

stories.title: Vocus hit by Australia Singapore Cable break
stories.summary: Vocus has reported disruptions due to a break in the Australia-Singapore cable, impacting internet connectivity in the region. This incident highlights the vulnerabilities in global communication infrastructure and the critical need for robust solutions to ensure uninterrupted service. The Australian tech ecosystem is closely monitoring the situation as it affects numerous businesses and consumers.

stories.title: Europe has its first commercial orbital rocket
stories.summary: Isar Aerospace has successfully launched Europe's first fully commercial orbital rocket, marking a significant milestone in the space industry. This achievement opens new avenues for commercial and institutional customers in Europe, providing a viable alternative to existing launch services. The successful launch from a Norwegian spaceport underscores the growing capabilities of European aerospace companies.

stories.title: Travis Kalanick’s Atoms might be getting into the robotaxi business
stories.summary: Travis Kalanick's startup, Atoms, is reportedly exploring opportunities in the robotaxi sector, potentially reshaping urban transportation. This move could signify Kalanick's return to the forefront of tech innovation, aiming to address the challenges of mobility in cities. The robotaxi market is gaining traction, and Atoms aims to capitalize on this growing demand.

stories.title: An AI hacking trick is now being used to split the word ‘funding’ in spam
stories.summary: A new AI hacking technique has emerged, utilizing invisible Unicode characters to manipulate text for phishing attacks. This method demonstrates the evolving tactics of cybercriminals, highlighting the need for advanced security measures in digital communications. Microsoft has identified this trend, emphasizing the importance of vigilance in cybersecurity practices.

stories.title: The Top Tech Trends at IFA Berlin 2026
stories.summary: The IFA Berlin 2026 showcased several cutting-edge tech trends, including advancements in smart home devices and AI integration. The event highlighted how technology is increasingly becoming intertwined with everyday life, pushing boundaries in consumer electronics. Innovations presented at the fair are expected to shape the market landscape in the coming years.
